{{Short description|American ichthyologist (1924–2020)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2014}}
'''John Ernest "Jack" Randall''' (May 22, 1924 – April 26, 2020) was an American [[ichthyologist]] and a leading authority on [[coral reef fish]]es. Randall described over 800 species and authored 11 books and over 900 scientific papers and popular articles.<ref name=NYT>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/05/29/science/john-e-randall-dead.html |title=John E. Randall, Ichthyologist Extraordinaire, Dies at 95 |author=John Schwartz |date=2020-05-29 |work=[[New York Times]] |access-date=2020-06-02}}</ref> He spent most of his career working in [[Hawaii]].<ref name=FWP>{{cite web|url=https://www.fishwisepro.com/Photographers/jack-randall-24|title=Photographer Jack Randall |work=FishWisePro |access-date=26 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fishwisepro.com/pictures/photographers/Jack-Randall-24|title=Pictures |work=FishWisePro |access-date=26 April 2020}}</ref> He died in April 2020 at the age of 95 <ref>[http://marineexploration.org/jack/ Remembering Jack Randall]</ref>

==Career==
John Ernest Randall was born in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] in May 1924, to John and Mildred (McKibben) Randall.<ref name="NYT" /> In high school he acquired a love of marine fish after a visit to the [[tide pools]] of [[Palos Verdes]] and, after serving stateside in the Medical Corps of the U.S. Army during the post-[[D-Day]] years of WWII,<ref name=AUAS>John Randall bio, The Academy of Underwater Arts & Sciences. (http://www.auas-nogi.org/bio_randall_john.html {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304120033/http://www.auas-nogi.org/bio_randall_john.html |date=March 4, 2016 }})</ref> received his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] degree from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1950. In 1955 he earned his [[Doctorate|Ph.D]] in ichthyology from the [[University of Hawaii]].<ref name=BishopMuseum/>

After spending two years as a research associate at the [[Bishop Museum]] in Honolulu, Hawaii, he moved to [[Miami]], [[Florida]] and worked briefly at the [[University of Miami]]'s Marine Laboratory,<ref name=Carpenter2005>Carpenter, K. E. & Pyle, R. (2005). Notice of award of Bleeker Award for Systematics</ref> alongside [[C. Richard Robins]] who remained there for his career.<ref name = ETYFish>{{cite web| url = https://etyfish.org/name-of-the-week/ | title = Name of the Week Richard (Dick) Robins (1928-2020) | access-date = 8 April 2021 | date = 7 April 2021 | author = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J. Lazara | website = ETYFish.org}}</ref> From 1961 to 1965 he worked as Professor of [[Zoology]] and also, from 1962 to 1965, as the director of the Institute of Marine Biology at the [[University of Puerto Rico]]. From 1965 to 1966 he served as the director of the Pacific Foundation of Marine Research's Oceanic Institute, [[Makapuu Point]], Hawaii. From 1966 to 1984 he worked as an ichthyologist at the Bishop Museum, becoming chairman of the museum's zoology department in 1975<ref name="NYT" /> and gaining the title of Senior Ichthyologist in 1984.<ref name=BishopMuseum>John Randall profile, Hawaii Biological Survey Staff, Hawaii Biological Survey ({{cite web|url=http://hbs.bishopmuseum.org/staff/randall.html |title=HBS Staff - Randall |access-date=2013-08-26 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130702070917/http://hbs.bishopmuseum.org/staff/randall.html |archive-date=July 2, 2013 }})</ref>  He concurrently served as a [[marine biologist]] at the Institute of Marine Biology, University of Hawaii.<ref name=Thaman2009>Thaman, R. R. (2009). Dau Qoli – "Jack" Randall – Life Scientist and Man for all (Fishing) Seasons. ''Island Life, September 2009''</ref>

In 2005 he was awarded the first Bleeker Award in Systematic Ichthyology at the Seventh Indo-Pacific Fish Conference in Taipei, Taiwan.<ref name=Carpenter2005/><ref>[http://australianmuseum.net.au/image/Dr-John-E-Randall/ Dr John E. Randall] [[Australian Museum]], August 9, 2013. Retrieved August 26, 2013. [https://web.archive.org/web/20131022191257/http://australianmuseum.net.au/image/Dr-John-E-Randall/ Archived here.]</ref><ref>[http://hbs.bishopmuseum.org/staff/randall.html John E. Randall, Ph.D.] Hawaii Biological Survey, April 4, 2005. Retrieved August 26, 2013. [https://web.archive.org/web/20130702070917/http://hbs.bishopmuseum.org/staff/randall.html Archived here.]</ref>

==Works==
* ''Fishes of the Gilbert Islands'', Atoll Res. Bull. 1955, No. 47 (xi - 243 pp.), Pac. Sci, Bd., Nat. Acad. Sci., Wash D. C.
* ''A Contribution to the Biology of the Acanthuridae (Surgeon Fishes)'' (1955, in Issue 10 of Theses for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy, University of Hawaii (Honolulu))
* ''A review of the labrid fish genus Labroides, with descriptions of two new species and notes on ecology.'' Pac. Sci.
* ''Let a Sleeping Shark Lie'', 1961
* ''Three New Butterflyfishes (chaetodontidae) from Southeast Oceania'', 1975
* (with Henri Lavondès) ''Les noms de poissons marquisiens'', 1978
* (with Roger Lubbock) ''Three New Labrid Fishes of the Genus Cirrhilabrus from the Southwestern Pacific'' (in Volume 25, Issue 2 of ''Occasional papers of the Bernice Pauahi Bishop Museum of Polynesian Ethnology and Natural History'', Bishop Museum Press, 1982)
* ''Caribbean Reef Fishes'', 1983
* ''Pomacanthus Rhomboides (Gilchrist and Thompson), the Valid Name for the South African Angelfish Previously Known as Pomacanthus Striatus'' (J.L.B. Smith Institute of Ichthyology, 1988, {{ISBN|978-0-86810-172-9}})
* ''Coastal Fishes of Oman'' (1995; {{ISBN|978-0-8248-1808-1}})
* ''Shore Fishes of Hawaii'' (1996; {{ISBN|978-0-939560-21-9}})
* ''Annoted Checklist of the Inshore Fishes of the Ogasawara Islands'' (in Volume 11 of ''National Science Museum monographs'', National Science Museum, 1997)
* (with Phillip C. Heemstra) ''Review of the Indo-Pacific Fish Genus Odontanthias (Serranidae: Anthiinae), with Descriptions of Two New Species and a Related New Genus'' in Volume 38 of ''Indo-Pacific fishes'', Bishop Museum, 2006
* (with Jeffrey W. Johnson) ''Revision of the soleid fish genus Pardachirus'', in ''Indo-Pacific fishes'', Bishop Museum, 2007
* (with William N Eschmeyer) ''Revision of the Indo-Pacific Scorpionfish Genus Scorpaenopsis: With Descriptions of Eight New Species'' in ''Indo-Pacific fishes''
* ''Revision of the Goatfish Genus Parupeneus (Perciformes: Mullidae) with Descriptions of Two New Species'' in ''Indo-Pacific fishes''
* (with Phillip C. Heemstra) ''Review of the Indo-Pacific Fishes of the Genus Odontanthias (Serranidae: Anthiinae), with Descriptions of Two New Species and a Related New Genus'' in ''[[Indo-Pacific fishes]]''
* (with Margaret M. Smith) ''[http://hdl.handle.net/10962/d1019709 A review of the Labrid fishes of the Genus Halichoeres of the Western Indian Ocean, with descriptions of six new species]'' in Ichthyological Bulletin of the J.L.B. Smith Institute of Ichthyology; No. 45. J.L.B. Smith Institute of Ichthyology, [[Rhodes University]]. (1982; {{ISBN|978-0-86810-071-5}})
* (with David W. Greenfield) ''[http://hdl.handle.net/10962/d1019863 A preliminary review of the Indo-Pacific Gobiid fishes of the genus Gnatholepis]'' in Ichthyological Bulletin of the J.L.B. Smith Institute of Ichthyology; No. 69. J.L.B. Smith Institute of Ichthyology, [[Rhodes University]]. (2001; {{ISSN|0073-4381}})
* Parenti, P. and J.E. Randall, 2000. An annotated checklist of the species of the labroid fish families Labridae and Scaridae. Ichthyol. Bull. J.L.B. Smith Inst. Ichthyol. (68):1-97.

* See [[:Category:Taxa named by John Ernest Randall]]

== Taxa named in his honor ==
Randall has had over 60 taxa named in his honor, among them are:<ref name = FishbaseNames>{{cite web |url=https://fishbase.us/Nomenclature/ScientificNameSearchList.php? |title=Scientific Names where Species Equals randalli |access-date=5 September 2023 |publisher=Fishbase}}</ref>
* ''[[Assessor randalli]]'' <small>[[Gerald R. Allen|Allen]] & [[Rudie Hermann Kuiter|Kuiter]], 1976</small>, '''Randall's assessor''' or '''Randall's devilfish''', is a species of [[ray-finned fish]] belonging to the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Plesiopidae]], the [[longfin]]s or roundheads. It is found in the western [[Pacific Ocean]].<ref name = ETYFish21>{{cite web | url = https://etyfish.org/cichliformes8/ | title = Order CICHLIFORMES: Families AMBASSIDAE, GRAMMATIDAE, PLESIOPIDAE, OPISTOGNATHIDAE, POLYCENTRIDAE, EMBIOTOCIDAE and PHOLIDICHTHYIDAE | accessdate= 30 August 2023 | author1 = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J. Lazara | name-list-style = amp | work = The ETYFish Project Fish Name Etymology Database | publisher = Christopher Scharpf and Kenneth J. Lazara | date = 23 August 2023}}</ref>
* ''[[Diplogrammus randalli]]'' <small>[[Ronald Fricke|R. Fricke]], 1983</small> (Randall's fold dragonet).
* '''Randall's snapper''', ''[[Randallichthys filamentosus]]'' <small>([[Pierre Fourmanoir|Fourmanoir]], 1970)</small> is a species of [[ray-finned fish]], a snapper belonging to the [[Family (biology)×|family]] [[Lutjanidae]]. It is native to the [[Indo-Pacific]] region.<ref name = ETYFish7>{{cite web | url = https://etyfish.org/lutjaniformes/ | title = Order LUTJANIFORMES: Families HAEMULIDAE and LUTJANIDAE | work = The ETYFish Project Fish Name Etymology Database | editor1 = Christopher Scharpf | editor2 = Kenneth J. Lazara | name-list-style = amp | date = 5 January 2021 | accessdate = 25 May 2021 | publisher = Christopher Scharpf and Kenneth J. Lazara | archive-date = April 12, 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210412135037/https://etyfish.org/lutjaniformes/ | url-status = dead }}</ref>
* ''[[Acanthopagrus randalli]]'', Middle East Black Seabream, <small>[[Yukio Iwatsuki|Iwatsuki]] & [[Kent E. Carpenter|Carpenter]], 2009</small>
* ''[[Gymnothorax randalli]]'', Randall's moray <small>[[David G. Smith (ichthyologist)|D. G. Smith]] & [[Eugenia Brandt Böhlke|E. B. Böhlke]], 1997</small>
* ''[[Plectranthias randalli]]'' <small>[[Pierre Fourmanoir|Fourmanoir]] & [[Jacques Rivaton|Rivaton]], 1980</small> is a species of [[fish]] in the family [[Serranidae]] occurring in the Western [[Pacific Ocean]].<ref name = ETYFish4>{{cite web | url = http://www.etyfish.org/perciformes4/ | title = Order PERCIFORMES (part 4): Suborder SERRANOIDEI: Families SERRANIDAE and ANTHIADIDAE | access-date= 30 March 2023 | author1 = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J. Lazara | name-list-style = amp | work = The ETYFish Project Fish Name Etymology Database | publisher = Christopher Scharpf and Kenneth J. Lazara | date = 22 September 2018}}</ref>
